{
  "claims": [

      "quantifications": "NA",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "NA",
      "modulator_temporal": "NA"

      "quantifications": "NA",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "NA",
      "modulator_temporal": "NA"

      "quantifications": "NA",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "NA",
      "modulator_temporal": "NA"
    },
    {

      "effect": "Changes in the monetary transmission mechanism",

      "modulator_uncertainty": "NA",
      "modulator_temporal": "When the economy/environment changes"

      "modulator_temporal": "NA"
    },
    {

      "modulator_uncertainty": "Perhaps",
      "modulator_temporal": "NA"

    {

      "modulator_temporal": "NA"

      "modulator_uncertainty": "Relies on financial markets",
      "modulator_temporal": "NA"
    },
    {

      "effect": "Household and firm behavior (borrowing, spending, pricing, investment) adjusts",

      "quantifications": "NA",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "NA",
      "modulator_temporal": "Subsequent to changes in financial conditions"

      "effect": "Output and prices",

      "quantifications": "NA",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "NA",
      "modulator_temporal": "Subsequent to behavioral adjustments"
    },
    {

      "document_reference": "Page 3, Section 2: What is the transmission mechanism?, footnote 2",
      "quantifications": "NA",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "Described as less direct policy tools",
      "modulator_temporal": "NA"
    },
    {
      "cause": "Factors outside of the central bank’s control and interactions among transmission channels",
      "effect": "Amplification or dampening of pass-through from a given policy choice",
      "linking_explanation": "Exogenous conditions and channel interactions (e.g., credit, exchange rate, expectations) can strengthen or weaken the effect of policy on financial conditions and the real economy.",
      "document_reference": "Page 4, following Chart 1, first paragraph",
      "quantifications": "NA",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "Can amplify or dampen",
      "modulator_temporal": "NA"
    },
    {
      "cause": "Change in the policy rate",
      "effect": "Exchange rate movements",
      "linking_explanation": "Policy-driven shifts in interest rate differentials alter currency valuations through capital flows and relative return channels.",
      "document_reference": "Page 4, following Chart 1, second paragraph",
      "quantifications": "NA",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "Presented as examples (such as the exchange rate)",
      "modulator_temporal": "NA"
    },
    {
      "cause": "Change in the policy rate",
      "effect": "Borrowing rates that firms and households face",
      "linking_explanation": "Bank funding costs and market yields adjust with the policy rate, passing through to loan and mortgage rates faced by the private sector.",
      "document_reference": "Page 4, following Chart 1, second paragraph",
      "quantifications": "NA",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "Presented as examples",
      "modulator_temporal": "NA"
    },
    {
      "cause": "Change in the policy rate",
      "effect": "Other asset prices",
      "linking_explanation": "Discount rates and risk premia adjust with policy changes, affecting valuations of equities, bonds, and other assets.",
      "document_reference": "Page 4, following Chart 1, second paragraph",
      "quantifications": "NA",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "Presented as examples",
      "modulator_temporal": "NA"
    },
    {
      "cause": "Non-instantaneous and heterogeneous pass-through of policy rate changes to financial variables",
      "effect": "Lags in monetary policy",
      "linking_explanation": "Different financial variables adjust at different speeds to policy changes, creating overall delays in how policy affects the real economy and inflation.",

      "quantifications": "NA",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "NA",
      "modulator_temporal": "Varies by financial variable"
